what: Release of a sphere sliding on a held sphere (Nov 18 item 5: how should the third ball move, and when may its velocity change?). Two spheres in 2D: the lower one on a nearly still plate (Gamma 1e-9), free to slide (frictionless hold), the upper one set down at rest at 10, 20 or 40 degrees from vertical. Closed form (frictionless, from horizontal momentum and energy): the pair's contact force vanishes at the angle given. Engine: method/held-contact 9860a26, mode sphere and mode fixed (b8d3e2a), v_hold 1e-2, dt_hold 5e-4, gap_release 1e-4; release sampled every 2e-4 time units.
reading: Motion on the sphere lets go within 0.04 degrees of the closed form at all three starting angles: holding the normal velocity at zero with tangential motion free gives the right horizontal and vertical velocities, and the right moment to let go (the force reaching zero).

The fixed-angle variant lets go 0.81 degrees after capture at every angle: the upper sphere moves on the tangent plane, the gap opens, and the gap rule (1e-4 D, a set constant) decides; it then falls back onto the lower sphere and is captured again at a new angle. Its release point is set by that constant, not by the force.
